messages.content: You are an expert space systems engineer providing detailed technical specifications.

You are an expert space systems engineer for Project Dyson, a non-profit
planning the construction of a Dyson swarm.

Provide a DETAILED technical proposal for: **Prospecting Survey and Rendezvous Scouts**
Context: Phase 0 - Space Resource Processing

## Phase 0 after the 2026 re-assessment (binding context)

The original Phase 0 plan (a central 50 kt/yr processing station at Sun–Earth L4/L5, crew visits,
production LOX/LH₂, 100 kW-class freighters) was found not to close and is abandoned. Design for the
revised architecture below. Do not re-propose the abandoned design.

### Agreed by all three re-assessment models
- Split Phase 0 into 0A (research + pathfinders) and gated 0B (industrial): Structure agreed; budgets → §3 (All three)
- Abandon 50 kt/yr central SEL4/L5 ore processing: — (All three)
- Co-locate at least beneficiation and primary processing at the target NEA; ship product, not ore: Reference architecture (All three. GPT: "favoured but not universally optimal". Claude retains a central station fed with ≥20:1 concentrate as an alternative. Gemini's own weighted QOC scores SEL1 marginally higher (see §6).)
- Narrow product to native/reduced Fe-Ni; defer solar-grade Si and oxide-derived Al/Si: Fe-Ni baseline; Al/Si pilot or deferred (All three)
- Delivered product scale of order 1 kt/yr: 0.6–2.5 kt/yr (Claude 0.6–2.2 (central 1.3); Gemini 1.0–2.5 (1.5, of which 0.3 is water); GPT 0.6–1.0 contracted (0.67–1.33 capacity))
- MW-class cargo tugs: 1.0–2.5 MWe each; 10–18 tugs; 150–300 t payload (→ §3 for point values)
- Robots powered by HV tether from site power, with onboard battery for mobility and safe-mode: 1–3 kV; battery 10–50 kWh (Claude 2–3 kV, 10–30 kWh; Gemini 1–3 kV, 15–25 kWh; GPT 20–50 kWh, voltage unspecified)
- Delete the 200–500 MWh Li-ion line; size storage per site: 0.5–15 MWh total (Claude 0.5–3 MWh + thermal; GPT 1.3–3.3 MWh; Gemini <15 MWh (YAML 10 MWh))
- Reject $5/W array pricing: Hardware ~$30–150/W, launch separately accounted (Claude $30–150/W hardware ($50–230 installed incl. launch); Gemini $60–100/W (spec $75, range $50–110); GPT $30–100/W allowance ($45–220 with delivery))
- Replace 32–50 × 100 kg monoprop prospectors: Remote survey + 4–10 EP rendezvous scouts of 200–600 kg (All three agree a monoprop bus has ~0.5–0.8 km/s Δv. Remote-survey method differs (→ §3).)
- Add an Earth-to-space launch/delivery line: Line agreed; magnitude → §3 (All three)
- Add a comms, ground segment and mission-operations line; DSN not assumed free: Line agreed (All three. Claude and GPT reject the round-1 2.5 TB/day (~230 Mbps) figure.)
- Phase 0 uncrewed; remove habitat and quarterly visits: 0 crew visits (All three. Claude and GPT reject the "human-rating" label in favour of structural reserve plus docking/servicing interfaces. Gemini keeps docking ports and structural margins without commenting on the label.)
- Add an EP propellant supply line; xenon not baselined: Line agreed; demand → §3 (All three)
- No production LOX/LH₂ in Phase 0: — (All three. Claude and GPT remove the EML1 depot; Gemini "defers" cryo depots to 0B/Phase 1.)
- Add NRE, pathfinder, spares and contingency lines: Lines agreed; values → §3 (All three)
- Write a full organization (bom-0-7) specification: ~$100–350M (Claude $100–300M; Gemini $150–250M (text $200M); GPT $150–350M)
- Add a debris/contamination requirement and budget tighter than 99%: $50–300M (Threshold → §3)
- Freeze one configuration-controlled baseline; mark legacy documents superseded: — (All three)
- Earth-supplied material as a fallback if microgravity metallurgy fails: — (All three. Ranking relative to lunar → §3.)
- Tie Phase 0 output to Phase 1 demand with a material/purity/date specification: — (All three)
- Add waste-heat rejection (radiators) explicitly: Item agreed; sizing → §3 (All three)

### Owner decisions
- D-01 (accepted 2026-10-12): Fund 0A. Hold 0B as a gated real option, sized at the gate by signed Phase 1 demand. Call Phase 0 a capability programme, not a cost saving.
- D-02 (accepted 2026-10-12): Hybrid: NASA life-cycle gates with TRL/AD² for each critical technology, plus four discriminating gates (target, demand, economics, licence). Stringency follows reversibility.
- D-03 (proposed; treat as interim): Set an ALARP requirement with an interim design ceiling. The number itself goes to modelling, tests and the licensing state.
- D-04 (proposed; treat as interim): Use SEL1 as the reference case. Re-decide jointly with Phase 1 at the 0B gate.
- D-05 (proposed; treat as interim): Select no propellant yet. Cost iodine as the reference case and argon as the alternate, pending the supply audit and life tests. Water EP stays a desk study until a C-type target is confirmed.

Under D-02, KDP-0B (the one-way commitment to 0B production) needs every project-ending technology
at TRL 6 in a relevant environment with no waivers; internal 0A milestones need TRL 4–5.

### This item: bom-0-1 Prospecting Survey and Rendezvous Scouts (0A)
Accepted scope: Remote survey (observing programme and survey data) plus electric-propulsion rendezvous scouts with subsurface sampling and bulk assay. Replaces the monopropellant prospector fleet.

Round-2 proposals for this item (per model; not approved as numbers):
- split/resize · bom-0-1 prospecting → remote survey + rendezvous scouts · supported by all · quantity: Claude 6 (4–8); Gemini 8 scouts + 2 telescopes; GPT 4–8 scouts · cost: scouts: Claude $30–80M; GPT $25–75M; Gemini $45–120M per unit (applied across 10 units incl. telescopes) · confidence: medium (Claude); high (Gemini); low (GPT)
- add · survey data / observing programme · supported by Claude, GPT · quantity: 1 · cost: Claude $20–60M; GPT $20–100M · confidence: low

Critical technologies (TRL re-baseline, panel envelope):
- T11 Rendezvous scout spacecraft (with sampling per Gemini and GPT): TRL 2–4 now, target 8, AD² 5–6, project-ending
- T18 Subsurface sampling and in-situ bulk grade assay: TRL 2–4 now, target 8, AD² 6, project-ending

Other Phase 0 items (do not duplicate their scope): bom-0-2 Mining Robots; bom-0-3 Processing Plant at the Target NEA; bom-0-4 MW-class Cargo Tugs; bom-0-5 Site Power, Arrays and Storage; bom-0-6 Water Pilot (C-type target only); bom-0-7 Organizational Infrastructure; bom-0-8 Earth-to-Space Launch and Delivery; bom-0-9 Communications and Ground Segment; bom-0-10 Mission Operations; bom-0-11 NRE, Ground R&D and Qualification; bom-0-12 0A Pathfinder Demonstrator; bom-0-13 Phase 1 Receiving Node (SEL1); bom-0-14 Spares and Replacements; bom-0-15 Debris and Contamination Control; bom-0-16 Electric-Propulsion Propellant Supply; bom-0-17 Contingency and Reserve.

State quantities and costs as ranges with their basis, split 0A and 0B where the item spans both,
and say where you disagree with the round-2 figures and why.

### Round-2 reconciliation for this item

# Reconciliation: bom-0-1 Prospecting Satellites (phase-0, round 2)

**Provenance caveat.** The panel's model attribution is still inconsistent. Each response's header names one model and its YAML `model:` field names another:

| Response header | YAML `model:` field |
|---|---|
| Claude Opus 5.5 | claude-opus-4-7 |
| Gemini 3.8 Flash | Claude-3.7-Sonnet-Thinking |
| GPT-6.1 Sol | GPT-5.2 |

In this reconciliation, **Claude**, **Gemini** and **GPT** refer to the response headers. The defect matters because two responses (Claude §1, GPT §1) argue that consensus regeneration depends on verified provenance.

Several responses also refer to round-1 positions by model name, for example "Claude's mixed fleet" in the Claude response and "Gemini favors 32" in the Gemini response. These are read as references to round-1 positions, not to the current authors.

---

## 1. Verdict matrix

| Finding | Claude | Gemini | GPT |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P0-F06**: 20 asteroids/sat/yr unreachable by a 100 kg craft | **agree** (on substance; disputes the title's causal claim) | **agree** | **partly** |
| **P0-F16**: consensus documents disagree with the BOM | **agree** | **agree** | **agree** (with evidence limitation) |

**P0-F06.** All three reject the 20/yr requirement as written.
- **Claude** and **GPT** both say spacecraft mass is not the binding constraint. Claude names per-target Δv, transfer time and geometry. GPT names transfer duration, thrust, geometry, navigation and dwell time.
- **GPT** alone holds that 20 remote observations per year is "not intrinsically impossible" and that no universal flyby limit has been established.
- **Gemini** accepts the finding fully. It argues that remote data from a small aperture is inadequate for characterisation.

**P0-F16.** All three confirm the prospecting discrepancy: 32 units / $160M in the BOM against 50 units / $250M in the consensus.
- **Claude** and **GPT** both say they could not verify the transport and ISPP discrepancies, because those specs were not supplied.
- **Claude** and **Gemini** additionally reject the $5M unit cost. Claude also objects to its "high" confidence label.
- **Claude** and **GPT** both reject "newer model version = authoritative".

---

## 2. Agreed changes

These are changes all three models support. Where values differ, the consolidated figure is the envelope of the three positions, with each model's nominal shown. No single value is selected.

| Change | Claude | Gemini | GPT | Consolidated |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Remove the "20+ asteroids/sat/yr" rate | yes | yes | yes | Remove |
| Redefine mission as rendezvous characterisation of externally pre-screened/shortlisted targets | yes | yes | yes | Rendezvous primary mode |
| Targets per craft | 2 (1–3) over life | 1 primary + 1 extended (1–2) | 1 primary, 2nd conditional on trajectory (1–2) | 1–2 baseline; Claude's upper bound 3 |
| Fleet reduced from 32/50 and gated in tranches | 12 (8–20); 2 pathfinders + 10 | 16 (12–24); 4 pathfinders + 12 | 16 as costing scenario only (8–32); 4 initial pathfinders | Gated tranches agreed; quantity **not** agreed (see §3) |
| Wet mass | 200 kg (170–250) | 210 kg (180–260) | 200 kg reference, pending mass closure (150–300) | ~200 kg nominal; 150–300 kg envelope |
| Main propulsion: solar-electric | ~1 kW Hall + monoprop/cold-gas RCS | Hall or gridded ion, Isp 1,800–3,000 s | SEP baseline + separate proximity control | EP main + separate proximity propulsion |
| Array power, BOL at 1 AU | 1.2 kW (1.0–1.8) | 1.4 kW (1.1–1.8) | 1.5 kW (1–2) | 1.2–1.5 kW nominal; 1.0–2.0 kW envelope |
| Spectral upper limit extended for the ~3 µm hydration band | 3.6 µm (3.2–4.3) | 3.6 µm (to 3.8) | ≥ ~3.2 µm (3.2–4.3) | ≥3.2 µm; 3.2–4.3 µm envelope |
| Hydration band ≠ proof of extractable water | yes | yes (raises solar-wind OH confound) | yes | Agreed |
| $5M unit cost unsupported; recurring unit cost | $22M (15–35) | $25M (18–35) | $12–25M recurring hardware | $12–35M envelope; scope differences noted in §4 |
| Prospectors self-powered; 0 MW from bom-0-5 | yes | yes | yes | 0 MW external |
| Primary mission life | 5 yr primary, 7 yr goal (5–8) | 3–5 yr primary | 3–5 yr primary, 7 yr goal | 3–5 yr primary (Claude: 5); 7 yr goal (Claude, GPT) |
| Add launch/injection, deep-space ground segment and ops, target-screening programme | separate lines | separate lines | inside an all-inclusive work package | Scope agreed; accounting treatment divergent |
| Spacecraft data products cross-interface to bom-0-2/0-3/0-6 lack specs (`in_bom: false`) | yes | yes | yes | Agreed |

---

## 3. Preserved divergences

### 3.1 Fleet size

**Claude: 12 (8–20).**
- Basis: ~2 commit-grade targets needed; pre-screen hit rate p = 0.15–0.30.
- Claude's binomial check gives P(≥2 hits) of 0.83 at n = 15 and 0.93 at n = 20, at p = 0.2.
- Assumes 70–85 % survival and 1.5–2.5 targets per surviving craft.
- Confidence: low.

**Gemini: 16 (12–24).**
- Basis: 85 % survival, 65 % qualification yield and 1.25 targets/craft give ≈ 11 qualified targets.
- Purpose: supply the target pool for 20 robots and 4 ISPP plants with 2–3 redundant sites.
- Its ACH judges 12 craft "vulnerable" to attrition.
- Confidence: medium.

**GPT: 16 as a costing scenario only (8–32); no quantity endorsed.**
- An illustrative binomial with q = 0.16 and ≥3 qualifying targets gives P = 48 % at N = 16 and 91 % at N = 32.
- GPT says this shows attrition and yield must enter sizing, but "does not justify 32".
- Confidence: low.

The models differ on the required number of commit-grade targets and the hit rate (see §5).

### 3.2 Pathfinder tranche

| Model | Position |
|---|---|
| Claude | 2 pathfinders |
| Gemini | 4 pathfinders |
| GPT | 4 initial (range 2–4) |

GPT's YAML records the old tranche as "5". No other response cites that figure.

### 3.3 Onboard Δv and propellant

| Model | Δv | Propellant | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude | 5.0 km/s (4–6.5) | 55 kg Xe/Kr | Two rendezvous at 1.5–3 km/s each + 10 % margin |
| Gemini | 3.2 km/s (2.5–4.2) | 65 kg | One primary rendezvous from C3 ≈ 0 with 30–40 % contingency |
| GPT | ~3 km/s (2–4) | ~30 kg (21–41) at 1,800 s | One primary target; explicitly "not a transfer solution" |

The difference tracks the targets-per-craft assumption.

### 3.4 Flyby tier vs all-rendezvous

**Claude.**
- Leans all-rendezvous, because remote triage is available externally (SPHEREx, NEO Surveyor, ground).
- Calls round 1's mixed fleet "defensible".
- Classifies the choice as a values trade-off.

**Gemini.**
- Favours all-rendezvous.
- Weighted score: 8.25 for all-rendezvous, 6.75 for mixed, 2.35 for flyby tour.
- Says flybys cannot provide thermal inertia, mass/density or fine-scale mineralogy.

**GPT.**
- Keeps flyby/mixed as "an alternative, not an agreed change".
- Calls it a values trade-off, provided both options have costed trajectories.
- Says no universal flyby yield limit has been established.

### 3.5 Throughput of non-rendezvous survey

- **Claude:** flyby rate ~0.5–1.5/yr. Remote triage gives tens to hundreds of objects per year but duplicates external assets.
- **Gemini:** flyby rate ~0.3–1.0/yr. Smallsat-aperture remote spectroscopy is inadequate for composition.
- **GPT:** 20/yr remote is not intrinsically impossible. Neither 20/yr nor a 0.5–1.5/yr flyby limit is established. Remote and flyby modes should be separately budgeted supplementary products.

### 3.6 Propellant choice

- **Claude: Kr or Xe.**
  - Flown iodine EP is ~1 mN class; at 1.1 mN on 180 kg, 2.5 km/s takes ~13 yr.
  - A ~1 kW iodine Hall thruster is not flight-proven.
  - Krypton is the more realistic commonality choice, at a tank-mass penalty.
  - Fleet Xe (~0.7 t) does not bind; commonality is "a logistics preference".
- **Gemini: Kr or I₂, high confidence.** The aim is to avoid xenon cost and scarcity. It treats commonality with bom-0-4 as an architecture standard, marked `in_bom: true`.
- **GPT: the xenon concern should "not automatically be inherited".** A sub-tonne allocation does not establish a bottleneck. Qualification, efficiency, storage and contamination matter more than commonality.

### 3.7 Downlink volume per target and ground time

| Model | Per-target volume | Ground time / rate |
|---|---|---|
| Claude | 0.5–3 GB | 10–50 kbps; ~3,000–6,000 antenna-h/yr fleet. Says round-1 50–200 GB/target "does not close" (100 GB at 100 kbps ≈ 93 days) |
| Gemini | 5–20 GB (YAML: 10 GB) | 10–50 kbps; 200 h/yr per satellite |
| GPT | 1–5 GB | ~220–1,110 antenna-h per target at 10 kb/s effective. Says the round-1 0.1–200 GB estimates cannot share one allocation |

### 3.8 Thermal-IR payload

- **Claude:** 8–14 µm microbolometer, 1–2 kg, medium confidence.
- **Gemini:** 8–14 µm uncooled microbolometer, medium confidence.
- **GPT:** trade a calibrated thermal radiometer against cost and power. No continuous 3–14 µm requirement.

### 3.9 Elemental/GRNS and lidar

- **Claude:** GRNS optional, rendezvous only.
- **Gemini:** treats GRNS (4–6 kg, weeks of integration, low altitude) as an open question alongside penetrators and impactors. Lists micro-lidar in its rendezvous option and "Level 4 proximity" autonomy.
- **GPT:** keep GRNS/lidar optional until sensitivity and accommodation close. Rejects adopting a 3–6 kg GRNS "from an asserted mass alone". Replaces autonomy level labels with testable scenarios.

### 3.10 Nav beacon for bom-0-2

| Model | Position |
|---|---|
| Claude | Optional, not baseline |
| Gemini | Lists a direct RF beacon interface |
| GPT | Not proposed |

### 3.11 Resource ground-truth step

- **Claude:** mandatory before the ~$10B station; $50–200M (judgement).
  - Cites OSIRIS-REx: OVIRS identified phyllosilicates, but the regolith's near-zero cohesion was not predicted.
  - Raises bom-0-2 unit 1 as a possibly cheaper demonstrator.
- **GPT:** needed before industrial commitment, but its architecture and cost are not established. The $50–200M allowance "is not a validated mission estimate".
- **Gemini:** proposes no ground-truth line. It gates bom-0-2 on prospecting orbital data and lists penetrators or impactors as possible options.

### 3.12 Gating of downstream procurement

- **Claude:** gate fabrication commitment of bom-0-2/0-3/0-6 on prospecting results 3–5 yr after launch. Long-lead design proceeds in parallel. ~75 % likely the better decision, medium confidence.
- **Gemini:** hard gate. bom-0-2 "cannot be built or deployed" until probes return orbital data.
- **GPT:** three evidence-based gates (A: fleet sizing; B: production expansion; C: industrial commitment). Gate C blocks irreversible procurement only. Rejects a fixed "3–5 year gate" as a forecast, not a pass criterion.

### 3.13 Authority after P0-F16

- **Claude:** the configuration-controlled BOM line is authoritative, changed via change requests. Consensus is a derived artefact stamped with BOM version and spec hashes.
- **GPT:** keep the current BOM as a record of the existing baseline, "not as proof that its quantities are correct". Mark the prospecting consensus superseded pending approval. Establish one configuration-controlled baseline with named technical authority.
- **Gemini:** does not address authority. Its P0-F16 change is a direct re-baseline to 16 units.

### 3.14 Cost scope and totals

| Model | Breakdown | Total |
|---|---|---|
| Claude | Recurring $15–35M; NRE $80–160M; line $260–580M; + launch $40–150M + ops $70–175M | Lifecycle ~$0.4–0.9B |
| Gemini | Recurring $25M → ~$400M hardware; + launch $120–180M + ground $100–150M + screening $15–30M | ACH quotes "$400M HW + $150M launch/ops" for 16 |
| GPT | Hardware $192–400M + development $80–160M + launch $60–180M + ops/screening $70–140M + 25–35 % reserve | All-inclusive $0.5–1.2B; phase total moves to $16.05–16.75B |

Only GPT carries an explicit reserve. Only GPT computes the phase-total effect.

### 3.15 Cost heritage figures cited

- **Claude:** MarCO ~$18.5M for two; SIMPLEx cap ~$55M, with Janus, Lunar Trailblazer and LunaH-Map overrunning or slipping.
- **Gemini:** MarCO ~$20M each; CAPSTONE ~$30M; Janus ~$50M for two; ESCAPADE ~$80M for two.
- **GPT:** SIMPLEx ~$55M cap excluding launch; Janus ~$49.7M award with no asteroid-operation heritage.

The two MarCO figures conflict (see Reviewer note).

### 3.16 Reversibility of the mission-mode decision

| Model | Classification |
|---|---|
| Claude | "Cheaply reversible on paper" |
| Gemini | "Type 1: irreversible commitment of payload and bus sizing" |
| GPT | "Partly irreversible once industrial assets are procured" |

## 6. Decision-quality audit

### D-A. Mission mode / redefinition of "survey"
(Claude D1, Gemini D1, GPT D1)

**Weakest link named.** The three models name three different links:
- **Claude: frame.** Round 1 asked "what kind of satellite" before "what information does the phase need, and is a fleet the cheapest source?"
- **Gemini: alternatives.** The original consensus assumed a high survey rate without trading rendezvous against remote observation.
- **GPT: values.** The required resource confidence and tolerated investment loss are missing.

**Missing or unsupported steps identified.**
- Claude: round 1 stated no criteria weights and never evaluated a null option (external data only).
- GPT: weights are "proposed discussion weights", not an agreed utility function. It avoids numerical scores as unsupported.
- Gemini provides numeric weighted scores (0.40/0.25/0.20/0.15).

**Certainty.**
- Claude: 20 rendezvous/yr feasible <1 %, high confidence.
- Gemini: impossible >99 %, high confidence.
- GPT: rendezvous at 20/yr "not a credible baseline". High confidence that spectra alone do not demonstrate extraction. Medium confidence that rendezvous improves characterisation.

**Trade-off and sensitivity reclassification.**
- Claude: mode is a sensitivity point (it drives Δv, mass and cost), not a trade-off point for the rate.
- Gemini: breadth vs depth is a trade-off point, "strongly" tilted to depth by false-positive cost. Target water fraction is a sensitivity point.
- GPT: depth vs speed/cost is "a genuine trade-off, not a fact to average". Dwell time is a sensitivity point.

**Falsifiers.**
- Claude: retrospective pre-screen hit-rate test.
- Gemini: 5-target ground-truth sampling.
- GPT: value-of-information study showing cheaper measurements give equivalent decisions.

### D-B. Fleet size and tranching
(Claude D2, Gemini D2, GPT D2)

**Weakest link: information (all three agree).** There is no target catalogue or trajectory study, and no hit-rate or reliability data.

**Missing or unsupported steps identified.**
- Claude: round 1 anchored on the BOM figure of 32.
- Claude: round 1 preserved Gemini's round-1 "high" confidence without flagging that it rested only on the number under review. Claude calls this a reasoning failure.
- Claude: round 1 admitted the information gaps but did not lower its confidence labels.
- Claude: notes Gemini's round-1 arithmetic error (32 × 1–2 ≠ 30–50).
- GPT: twelve, sixteen and thirty-two are "options, not evidence-derived answers".
- GPT: the previous reconciliation substituted "an envelope of opinions for a decision basis".

**ACH outcomes.**
- Claude: H2 (8–20) is least disconfirmed.
- Gemini: H2 (16) is "consistent" on budget and attrition; H3 (12) is "vulnerable".
- GPT: GRADE EtD shows strong evidence that the old count is unsupported, but weak evidence for any replacement.

**Trade-off reclassification.**

**Basis.** 2026 USD. Costs come from analogy and engineering judgement unless a calculation is shown.

**Scope.** This proposal addresses the accepted scope: a remote survey (observing programme and survey data) plus electric-propulsion (EP) rendezvous scouts with subsurface sampling and bulk assay. It replaces the monopropellant prospector fleet.

**Provenance.** The round-2 reconciliation describes a 12–16 × ~200 kg remote-sensing fleet. That predates the binding re-scope to 4–10 scouts of 200–600 kg with subsurface sampling. I treat the reconciliation's sizing as superseded and use its analyses only where they still apply.

---

| Remote survey | Observing programme plus data analysis. **No dedicated telescopes.** | 1 programme, 2027–2038 | Existing assets cover the pre-screen. Medium confidence. |

| Scout wet mass (iodine reference) | **550 kg** | 460–600 kg | Bottom-up budget, 15 % system margin (§4.3). Medium confidence. |

My position on the round-2 figures:
- I agree with Claude's quantity of 6 (range 4–8).
- I disagree with every round-2 unit cost as too low for a craft that carries a subsurface sampler. My figure is about $100M per scout fully amortised and $50–75M recurring.

---

## 1. Design philosophy

### 1.1 What decision this item exists to support

bom-0-1 serves one decision: the **Target gate** (one of the four D-02 discriminating gates) before KDP-0B. It does not exist to discover asteroids, catalogue taxonomy, or do science.

The question at that gate is whether at least one named NEA has:
- a **recoverable** Fe-Ni grade,
- regolith mechanics,
- spin state, and
- tug accessibility

that together let bom-0-2, bom-0-3 and bom-0-4 close at 0.6–2.5 kt/yr, with stated confidence, plus one backup.

Every instrument, kilogram and dollar below is justified against that question.

### 1.2 Why remote data alone cannot answer it (the null option)

I evaluated the null option: external data only, no scouts. **I reject it.** Remote data can tell us "S-type, radar-bright, about 15 % metal by meteorite analogy." It cannot tell us the four things the plant and robots depend on:

1. **Recoverable metal fraction and liberation.** How much metal reports to a magnetic concentrate after comminution, and at what grain size. This governs the processing plant's mass balance and is invisible remotely.
2. **Sulphur and phosphorus deportment.** Troilite (FeS) intergrown with metal sets the refining burden.
3. **Regolith depth, cohesion and grain-size distribution, top 1 m.** OSIRIS-REx is the cautionary datum: OVIRS identified phyllosilicates correctly, but nobody predicted the near-zero cohesion. The TAG head sank ~0.5 m.
4. **Spatial variability.** Grade at the 10–100 m scale over the area actually mined.

The value-of-information case is straightforward. bom-0-1 costs about $0.7–1.0B. 0B commits multiple billions in irreversible hardware to one rock. Cutting false-commit probability by even 10–20 percentage points pays for this item.

### 1.3 Opinionated principles

1. **Ground truth, not breadth.** Breadth is already bought by the world: SPHEREx, NEO Surveyor, Rubin, Gaia and IRTF. We pay for depth.
2. **Measure what the plant measures.** The core assay is a miniature beneficiation test: sieve, magnetic separation, weigh, then XRF the concentrate. A spectrum that must be converted to grade through a meteorite model is not enough.
3. **Put sampling risk on a cheap expendable, not the propulsion bus.** The mothership never touches down. SAPs land, anchor, core, assay and hop.
4. **Gate by evidence, not by calendar.** I adopt GPT's evidence-based gates. Tranche 2 is sized after tranche 1 has actually cored.
5. **Do not let scouts drive the propellant decision (D-05).** Fleet propellant is under 1 t against hundreds of tonnes for the tugs. Scouts can, however, be the first in-space data point for kW-class iodine Hall operation. That is useful to bom-0-4, so I exploit it with a fallback.
6. **Data-buy compatible.** Every scout requirement is written as a data-delivery requirement as well as a hardware requirement. That lets a commercial provider bid fixed-price "delivered assay per target."

---

I traded five approaches:

1. **Touch-and-go on the mothership** (OSIRIS-REx style): top ~5 cm only, one shot, and it puts the propulsion bus at risk. **Rejected.**
2. **Kinetic impactor** (Hayabusa2 SCI): exposes ~1 m strata, but the material is then remote-sensed, not assayed. It also produces large ejecta, which conflicts with bom-0-15. **Rejected as baseline.**
3. **Penetrator:** gives mechanics but recovers no sample to assay. **Rejected.**
4. **Pneumatic sampler** (PlanetVac-type, flown on the Moon in 2025): excellent in loose regolith. It needs gas, and its depth is limited to ~10–30 cm. **Retained as a secondary/backup head** for shallow grab samples if the drill stalls.
5. **Anchored lander with rotary-percussive drill to 1 m: BASELINE.**
   - It matches the mining robots' working depth.
   - It gives a stratigraphic profile.
   - Its contact forces and power draw are themselves geotechnical data for bom-0-2.

**Anchoring is the critical risk.** Philae's harpoons failed, and the lander bounced. Mitigations:
- Low-reaction screw anchors (3 legs).
- Cold-gas hold-down thrust during drilling (~0.5 N, short bursts).
- A drill reaction-torque limit that keeps stall torque below anchor capacity.
- Weight on bit of ≤ 5 N.

The drill needs to reach only 1 m. It must handle cohesionless granular material up to centimetre clasts. If it meets a boulder or monolith, it relocates by hopping.

### 5.3 Assay cell: "beneficiation in a box"

Process per core interval (four intervals per core: 0–10, 10–30, 30–60, 60–100 cm; 20–60 g each):

1. **Centrifuge-assisted sieving** at 0.5–1 g artificial gravity. Size fractions: < 0.1, 0.1–0.5, 0.5–2, > 2 mm. This gives the grain-size distribution.
2. **Crush** the > 2 mm fraction to < 1 mm (mini jaw/roll). This gives a liberation proxy.
3. **Magnetic separation** with a permanent-magnet drum (~0.3 T) in the centrifuge. Products: magnetic and non-magnetic fractions.
4. **Mass measurement** of each fraction with a resonant/inertial balance (works in microgravity), target ±2 % of fraction mass.
5. **Micro-XRF** on each fraction: Fe, Ni, Co, S, P, Si, Mg, Ca, Cr. This yields Ni/Co in metal, and S in concentrate (troilite carry-over).
6. **NIR microscope** (MicrOmega-class) for silicate mineralogy and hydrated phases.
7. **Evolved-gas analysis.** Stepped heating to 1,000 °C with a quadrupole mass spectrometer: H₂O, CO₂, SO₂/H₂S, organics. This is essential for C-types (bom-0-6) and for S.
8. **Contact gamma/neutron spectrometer** (CeBr₃ + He-3-free neutron detector, ~3 kg). It integrates 3–7 days per site for bulk Fe/Ni/H over ~0.3–0.5 m depth. This is the bulk check against the core-scale assay. **Option to delete** at PDR if the mass budget fails.

**Primary output:** *recoverable metal fraction (wt %) of run-of-mine regolith after < 1 mm comminution and single-pass magnetic separation, with concentrate composition*. This is the number bom-0-3 needs.

## 7. Fleet sizing and tranching

### 7.1 Requirement

**P(≥ 2 commit-grade Fe-Ni targets) ≥ 0.85**: one primary plus one backup.

A C-type for bom-0-6 is **opportunistic, not sized for**. bom-0-6 is conditional on a C-type target, and forcing one into the fleet would add ~2 scouts for a pilot that may never proceed.

### 7.2 Model

Characterised targets n = N × s × k, where:
- s = 0.8 is scout survival through the primary campaign (first-of-kind deep-space EP smallsat class; my judgement),
- k = 1.6 is targets per surviving scout (1 + 0.6 secondary),
- p is the probability that a pre-screened shortlist target proves commit-grade.

| p (pre-screen hit rate) | n for P(≥ 2) ≥ 0.85 | Scouts N |
|---|---|---|
| 0.5 | 6 (P = 0.89) | **4–5** |
| 0.4 | 8 (P = 0.89); 7 gives 0.84 | **6** |
| 0.3 | 10 (P = 0.85) | **8** |

**Caveats.** Hits are not independent. We visit best candidates first (which helps), and the pre-screen model may share systematic errors (which hurts). The A5 validation and tranche-1 results are the only defences. That is why the fleet is tranched.

### 7.3 Tranches

| Tranche | Units | Launch | Gate to proceed |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 pathfinders | 2 | 2031 | KDP-C for scouts (CDR passed, iodine/argon decision made) |
| T2 | 2–6 (nominal 4) | 2034 | **Gate A**: T1 has cored ≥ 1 m and assay repeatability is shown. N for T2 is recomputed from posterior p. |
| 0B option | 0–2 | ≥ 2037 | 0B gate: Phase 1 demand requires a second site, or the primary needs re-confirmation |

## 10. Contamination, debris and planetary protection (inputs to bom-0-15, D-03)

- **Planetary protection:** NEA targets are COSPAR Cat I–II. There is no sample return.
- **Assay integrity:**
  - Green-monoprop exhaust contains H₂O, CO₂ and N₂, which would corrupt hydration and C measurements. Rules: cold gas only below 500 m; witness plates on each SAP; full exhaust log.
  - Main EP plume (iodine deposition on optics and arrays, and on the surface) is excluded within 20 km during campaigns.
- **Ejecta:** escape speed at a 500 m body is ~0.2–0.3 m/s. Drilling, hopping and landing can loft material above it.
  - **Proposed interim ceiling for this item:** ≤ 100 g per site liberated above escape speed; no particles > 1 cm intentionally lofted.
  - The final number belongs to bom-0-15 under ALARP.
- **End of life:** scouts either remain as sentinels and are then disposed to a heliocentric orbit with no close approach to the target or SEL1 within 100 yr, or make a controlled landing outside the designated mining area. The choice is made with bom-0-15.
